event.text:
I reproduced the sweep failure and found it wasn't a code bug in either "Chosing models" task: `npm test` spawns one worker process per test file (98 of them), and on this machine that reliably starves some workers mid-startup on Windows, producing exactly the errors in the output (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')`, `Vitest failed to find the runner`) on a random subset of files each run — a single narrowed test always passed, and a second full run passed all but one unrelated file with a Windows `EPERM` rename race, confirming it's spawn-storm flakiness, not a rule violation.

Fix: set `isolate: false` in `vitest.config.mts` so files reuse workers instead of spawning one per file (vitest's own run output was already hinting at this). Ran the full `npm test` four times afterward — all four passed cleanly (96 passed, 2 skipped, 1188 tests passed, 3 skipped), with no spawn-related errors.

Neither of the board's two tasks ("Choosing a model for each phase of a plan", "Switching model in a chat session") owns any of the files named in the failure output, and this fix doesn't touch their delivered rules, so per the instructions I left the board as-is (both remain `tested`).
